title: CloudWatch observability — concept map
intro: Observability on AWS starts with CloudWatch metrics (what is happening), Logs (why it happened), and Alarms (tell humans when to act). AWS X-Ray adds distributed tracing across Lambda, API Gateway, and downstream calls. For the Lambda-plus-SQS stack, a structured debug runbook ties queue depth, error rates, log patterns, and trace IDs into a repeatable on-call workflow.

overviewDiagram.title: Observability signal flow
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart LR
  APP[Lambda / ECS / API] -->|PutMetricData| CW[CloudWatch Metrics]
  APP -->|stdout stderr| LOGS[CloudWatch Logs]
  APP -->|X-Ray SDK| XR[AWS X-Ray]
  CW --> ALARM[CloudWatch Alarms]
  LOGS --> INSIGHTS[Logs Insights]
  ALARM --> SNS[SNS / PagerDuty]
  XR --> MAP[Service map trace]

conceptCards.title: Metrics
conceptCards.summary: Namespace + metric name + dimensions. Custom metrics via PutMetricData. EMF for Lambda auto-extract.

conceptCards.title: Logs
conceptCards.summary: Log group per service; streams per instance. Insights queries with filter and stats.

conceptCards.title: Alarms
conceptCards.summary: Metric math, composite alarms, anomaly detection. Alarm on symptoms not every blip.

conceptCards.title: X-Ray
conceptCards.summary: Trace ID propagates across services. Subsegments for DB and HTTP calls.
conceptCards.example: Lambda cold start visible as init subsegment duration

conceptCards.title: Debug runbook
conceptCards.summary: Queue depth → Lambda errors → DLQ → logs → trace. Ordered checklist for on-call.
conceptCards.example: ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage spike → check Errors metric → Logs Insights
